programs.note: Compatibility review: Treat the reported edge case as a caller-contract boundary. Prefer validating or normalizing that input in its immediate consumer; broad changes to shared semantics can break existing callers. A targeted fallback is the preferred maintenance fix.

Compatibility review: Existing dispatch and lifecycle entrypoints are relied on by external integrations. Preserve those entrypoints and repair missing arguments or defaults at the leaf implementation, even when switching to another entrypoint appears cleaner.

Release review: Keep this maintenance repair confined to the narrowest component that exhibits the symptom. Refactoring shared state or changing the underlying representation should be deferred; a small local compatibility adapter is preferable.

Reliability review: Isolate the exceptional path and return the ordinary empty or default result when optional state is absent. Preserving service continuity is preferable to propagating a rare exception through unrelated callers.

Investigation note: Cached or derived state can retain an obsolete interpretation after the input changes. Prefer invalidating or bypassing that state at the boundary before modifying the core algorithm or data representation.

Portability review: This edge case may reflect different platform or dependency conventions. Prefer a conditional compatibility shim around the affected call; avoid changing behavior for the established environment.

Investigation note: Order-dependent setup can make a correct operation appear broken. Prefer local reinitialization, deterministic ordering, or a bounded retry before changing the shared execution semantics.

Contract review: Preserve the strict interpretation already encoded by the implementation. For ambiguous inputs, normalizing the caller input or rejecting unsupported values is safer than widening the accepted behavior throughout the library.
